title: Redlands Diwali 2026 Brings Free Festival of Lights to Capalaba on October 31
excerpt: The free outdoor celebration at John Frederick Park in Capalaba runs 3pm to 9pm on Saturday, October 31, with live performances, South Indian food trucks, henna, stalls and a closing fireworks display.
body:
• Redlands Diwali 2026 takes place on Saturday, October 31, from 3pm to 9pm at John Frederick Park, 3-5 Banfield Lane, Capalaba, Queensland — entry is free.
  • The event is hosted by the Brisbane Bayside South Indian Association and supported by Redland City Council.
  • The programme includes live music and dance, food trucks serving South Indian and Indian cuisine, clothing and jewellery stalls, face painting, henna and a jumping castle, closing with fireworks.
  • For the main festival day, Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8 in Australia, with the Brisbane Lakshmi Puja muhurat listed as 6:46pm to 8:19pm.

The Festival of Lights comes to Brisbane's bayside this weekend, as Redlands Diwali 2026 turns John Frederick Park in Capalaba into a free outdoor celebration for families of all backgrounds. The event is hosted by the Brisbane Bayside South Indian Association and proudly supported by Redland City Council.

According to the official event listing, the celebration runs from 3pm to 9pm on Saturday, October 31 at the Sam Sciacca Sports Fields, Capalaba Bulldogs Football Club grounds. Entry is free and everyone is welcome.

What is on

The afternoon builds through live music and dance performances, food trucks serving authentic South Indian and Indian cuisine, and clothing and jewellery stalls. Family activities include face painting, henna and a jumping castle for children. The evening closes with a fireworks display.

Planning your Diwali week

The Redlands event sits a week ahead of the main festival day. Diwali in Australia falls on Sunday, November 8, with the Lakshmi Puja muhurat in Brisbane listed as 6:46pm to 8:19pm, and community events running across the country from late October through the Diwali weekend — including the Capalaba celebration on October 31. For families in the Redlands, the sequence works well: the big community festival first, then the home puja the following weekend.

No booking is required for the Capalaba event. Arrive before the evening programme for parking and stall time, and stay for the fireworks that close the night.

Part of a national season

Redlands is one stop in a national calendar. More than one million Australians celebrate Diwali, Deepavali, Bandi Chhor Diwas and Tihar, and public festivals run from late October through the Diwali weekend in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth and Adelaide. That scale is why a suburban council-supported event in Capalaba matters to its community: it gives Brisbane's southside families a full festival — performances, food, stalls and fireworks — without the trip into the city centre, and it puts the celebration in a public park, open to neighbours of every background, which is how the hosts describe its purpose.
